title: Total Waviness of Numbers in Range I
summary: Given two integers num1 and num2, calculate the total waviness of all numbers in the inclusive range [num1, num2].
statement: Given two integers num1 and num2, calculate the total waviness of all numbers in the inclusive range [num1, num2]. Waviness is the count of peaks and valleys in each number, where a peak is a digit greater than both neighbors and a valley is a digit less than both neighbors. The first and last digits cannot be peaks or valleys, and numbers with fewer than three digits have a waviness of zero.
constraints: A middle digit contributes one when it is strictly greater than both neighbors or strictly less than both.
Sum this waviness across the inclusive range.
hints: Only internal digit positions can be peaks or valleys.
Enumerate the modest numeric range, convert each value to digits, and compare every internal digit with its two neighbors.
Add one for either strict greater-than-both or strict less-than-both.
Each qualifying position is examined once and the endpoint exclusions follow directly from the loop bounds.
editorial: Each qualifying position is examined once and the endpoint exclusions follow directly from the loop bounds.

tests.explanation: Only 120, 121, and 130 contribute one each, totaling three.
Digits eight and four are a peak and valley, so the waviness is two.
